title: Video Strategy
article_body:
Video is the closest thing businesses have to a conversation at scale. When someone watches a video of a subject matter expert explaining how something works, walking through a comparison, or sharing what a customer experienced, they're not just gathering information — they're forming a relationship. They're deciding whether they trust you before they ever reach out.

Most companies underuse video entirely, or they produce video without a strategy. They create a brand overview once, post it on their homepage, and consider the job done. That's not a video strategy. A video strategy means creating the right types of videos, optimizing them for the right platforms, and deploying them at the right moments in the sales and marketing process.

## The Two Video Frameworks

The Endless Customers approach to video is built around two complementary frameworks. The Selling 7 covers the seven types of videos that most directly support the sales process: cost and price videos, the 80% video, product and service fit videos, landing page videos, customer journey videos, bio videos, and claims we make videos. These are the videos that shorten sales cycles, build individual trust, and move prospects from consideration to commitment.

The Big 5 applied to video extends the same content topics that drive trust in written articles — cost, problems, comparisons, reviews, and best-in-class — into video format for YouTube and social. These videos drive discovery. They reach buyers who are in the research phase and haven't yet found you, building awareness and trust at scale.

## Long-Form and Short-Form Serve Different Goals

Long-form video (typically five to twenty minutes) is where depth lives. YouTube is the home for long-form video content. These videos educate buyers thoroughly, answer complex questions, and build the kind of trust that comes from someone spending real time with your thinking. Long-form is especially effective for existing audiences who want to go deeper.

Short-form video (typically 5 to 90 seconds) is where awareness lives. YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, TikTok, and Facebook Reels are the platforms. Short-form reaches new audiences, expands brand visibility, and works as a top-of-funnel discovery tool. The average person watches over an hour of short-form video per day. If your buyers are in that population — and they almost certainly are — short-form is a channel you can't ignore.

The smartest approach is to plan content that can live in both formats. A 15-minute YouTube video on the cost of your service generates five to ten short-form clips that can run across social for weeks. Your long-form content investment multiplies when you build a repurposing workflow from the start.

## YouTube as a Core Channel

YouTube is the second-largest search engine in the world and one of the most effective paths to appearing in Google search results. Studies suggest YouTube videos are fifty times more likely to appear in Google results than written content. For companies trying to be found by buyers who are actively researching, YouTube is a search channel as much as it is a social one.

Your YouTube channel should be treated with the same level of care as your website: consistent branding, organized playlists, optimized titles and descriptions, and a regular publishing cadence. A channel that hasn't been updated in six months doesn't inspire trust. One that publishes consistently, answers real buyer questions, and features the actual people buyers will work with is one of the most powerful trust assets a business can build.

## The Investment Required

Executing a serious video strategy requires people, equipment, and consistency. For most Endless Customers companies, this means hiring a full-time in-house videographer. The role covers production, editing, distribution, and the ongoing creation of new content across all formats. A skilled videographer working inside your business, surrounded by your subject matter experts, can produce a volume and quality of content that no outsourced agency or part-time arrangement can match.

Companies that commit to this investment consistently see shorter sales cycles, higher close rates, and dramatically stronger brand recognition. The ones that treat video as a nice-to-have remain dependent on cold outreach, trade shows, and referrals to fill their pipeline. The gap between those two outcomes is one dedicated video hire and a clear content plan.

what_youll_learn: Video is now the most effective trust-building medium online. Businesses that avoid it are leaving significant trust and revenue on the table.
There are two primary video frameworks in Endless Customers: The Selling 7 for sales-driven content and The Big 5 applied to video for marketing reach.
YouTube is the second-largest search engine in the world. Treating it like an afterthought means missing one of the most valuable discovery channels available.
Short-form vertical video (YouTube Shorts, Reels, TikToks) is where attention is concentrated today. It works differently from long-form and requires its own strategy.
Structure matters as much as content. Videos without a clear hook, flow, and payoff lose viewers quickly regardless of topic quality.
Most companies produce too few videos, use the wrong types, and deploy them in the wrong places. Getting this right is one of the highest-leverage activities in the Endless Customers system.

key_questions.question: How much video production quality is required?
key_questions.answer: Your videos don't need to be Hollywood productions, but they do need to be clear, well-lit, and audible. Poor audio is the most common reason viewers stop watching. You don't need expensive equipment, but a proper microphone and decent lighting are non-negotiable.

key_questions.question: Who should be on camera?
key_questions.answer: Your salespeople, subject matter experts, and company leaders. The people your buyers will eventually work with. Bio videos, sales support videos, and educational content are most effective when delivered by the people who actually know the subject. Video creates a relationship before the first meeting.

key_questions.question: Where should our videos live?
key_questions.answer: On YouTube as a primary home, embedded on your website's relevant pages, and distributed through short-form clips on social media. Every long-form video can generate multiple short-form clips for Reels, Shorts, and TikTok.

key_questions.question: How often should we publish videos?
key_questions.answer: Consistency matters more than frequency. One well-made video per week, published consistently, will outperform a burst of videos followed by silence. Commit to a cadence you can sustain.

key_questions.question: Does video content apply to B2B companies?
key_questions.answer: Yes, and in many cases B2B companies benefit more because their competitors are less likely to be doing video well. B2B buyers research purchases extensively, and video gives them a way to evaluate your team, your thinking, and your approach before they ever have a conversation.
